title: Bind supervisor intake to verified Python dependencies through existing bootstrap and promotion flow
rework_note: Third rework, after Human/Ops rejected the second rework's exact published PR #5599 head 68e2277aa33b53f4f95e7d6aebac521dc75178c3 (finding at /tmp/pantheon-python-provisioning-owner-review-20260905.md, extending the prior PR comment 5548960716 that had already asked for one policy owner). That rejection kept every fix from the second rework (packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet, read-only same-SHA reuse, isolated-then-publish) and found one more real defect: (7) the environment provisioning/reuse/publication policy from the second rework's fix for defect 6 was implemented twice -- scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh (~lines 143-239) and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh (~lines 404-487) each independently decided whether to reuse an existing environment, created a temporary venv, invoked pip, preflighted it, rejected an existing invalid destination, and performed the no-clobber renameat2 publication -- the exact mechanism the original failure already showed can drift between the bootstrap and sync paths, implemented twice instead of once. Fixed by moving that whole decision loop into one existing owner: ensure_supervisor_python_environment(), a new function in scripts/provision_live_supervisor_config.py (already the shared preflight/config-render module both entrypoints call into), exposed via a new --ensure-python-environment CLI mode. Both scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh now call that one CLI mode with their own --command-root/--python-parent/--requirements and read the reported python_executable/reused JSON fields; neither re-implements reuse, install, preflight, or publish. No second launcher, dispatcher, or cron was added, and bootstrap's keypair sequencing and sync's runtime/candidate selection remain at their existing entrypoints, per the reviewer's constraint.

owned: supervisor Python interpreter selection and dependency preflight (provision_live_supervisor_config.py, promote_supervisor_runtime.py)
scoped .orchestrator/requirements.txt dependency contract for the supervisor runtime only

single-owner environment provisioning/reuse/publication policy (ensure_supervisor_python_environment in provision_live_supervisor_config.py), consumed as thin callers by scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh, now per-candidate-SHA rather than one fixed path
a real subprocess signed dev-bridge packet intake test under a bootstrap-style venv (.orchestrator/development_bridge/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_bootstrap_python_runtime.py)
not_changing: scripts/ai_status.py, task archive, and TaskStore (owned by the separate archive-reconciliation prerequisite)
signed packet validation, bridge signing keys, or dev-bridge intake logic itself
supervisor tick-level imports or a second dispatcher/cron/launcher
scripts/supervisor_watchdog_install.py (already restarts from the recorded watchdog.supervisor_command, requires no interpreter-selection change)
composes_with: root-coordinated exact-version governed promotion on the live host after merge

failure_reproduction.case: On 2026-09-05 the live promoted supervisor (PID 96329, source 20282eba2ce2304560ab7eab0cd27af824a22b8b) launched with /usr/bin/python3 -- which has cryptography but not pydantic -- so the main loop stayed healthy while every dev-bridge packet drain failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic'.
root_causes: scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh never passed --python to promote_supervisor_runtime.py, so it defaulted to sys.executable (the ambient interpreter running the bootstrap/sync script itself)

scripts/provision_live_supervisor_config.py resolved --python with Path(...).resolve(), which fully dereferences a venv's bin/python symlink chain back to the base interpreter before CPython's own pyvenv.cfg lookup can run, silently losing every venv-provided package even when a venv path was explicitly passed

(found in review, fixed in rework) scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh generated the dev-bridge Ed25519 keypair -- which imports cryptography -- using the ambient python3 before the supervisor venv was ever created, so a fresh host with no ambient cryptography could not bootstrap at all

(found in review, fixed in rework) validate_python_dependencies() called importlib.metadata.version() only: it never parsed or enforced the requirements.txt version specifier and never imported the module, so a wrong-version or broken-native-extension install could report a passing preflight

(found in review, fixed in rework) scripts/sync-dev-root.sh pip-installed every promotion into one fixed $PANTHEON_DEPLOY_ROOT/runtime/supervisor-python directory -- the same directory a currently running incumbent supervisor had already launched from -- before any preflight ran, so a partial or failed install could break the live incumbent regardless of whether the candidate was ever accepted
failure_reproduction.reproduction: test_cli_preserves_a_venv_symlink_path_instead_of_resolving_it (scripts/test_provision_live_supervisor_config.py) builds a real filesystem symlink to sys.executable and proves the pre-fix .resolve() call would have collapsed it; test_validate_python_dependencies_rejects_a_de_virtualized_interpreter proves the base /usr/bin/python3 on this host fails the same pydantic-dependency preflight that was silently bypassed live; test_bare_venv_without_the_dependency_contract_fails_closed (new, see below) proves a venv built the same way as bootstrap/sync but never given .orchestrator/requirements.txt fails the real signed-packet drain instead of looking healthy.

implementation.dependency_contract: .orchestrator/requirements.txt pins pydantic>=2.9,<3, cryptography>=42,<51, and (new in this rework) packaging>=23,<27 -- the supervisor's own bridge/task-store imports plus the PEP 440 specifier authority the preflight probe itself now needs, not the product BFF's full dependency set.
implementation.interpreter_selection_fix: provision_live_supervisor_config.py stores Path(args.python).expanduser().absolute() instead of .resolve(), preserving a venv invocation path so CPython's own symlink-chasing pyvenv.cfg lookup still runs at supervisor launch. (Unchanged this rework.)
implementation.dependency_preflight: validate_python_dependencies() in provision_live_supervisor_config.py parses each requirements.txt line into (distribution_name, specifier), then runs a probe entirely inside the exact candidate interpreter that (a) calls importlib.metadata.version() for the real installed version, (b) enforces the declared specifier with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet -- the standard PEP 440 authority (new in this rework: the prior self-contained numeric-prefix comparator silently accepted 2.9rc1 against >=2.9,<3, accepted 2.9 against >=2.9.post1, and accepted the invalid specifier >=not-a-version by comparing against 0), and (c) calls importlib.import_module() on the package -- so a wrong version or a broken native extension (e.g. an unloadable pydantic_core) fails the preflight instead of passing on metadata alone. The --validate-python-dependencies-only CLI mode runs just this check without requiring --repo-config/--live-config/--status-root. Wired into provision's CLI (_main_locked) before any config write, and into promote's render_v2_config() before _replace_supervisor_locked's try block, so a failed preflight raises before the incumbent supervisor, live config, leases, or watchdog/cron binding are touched.
implementation.same_sha_reentry_preservation: New in this rework, moved from two independent implementations into one: ensure_supervisor_python_environment() in provision_live_supervisor_config.py validates an existing per-SHA supervisor Python environment read-only (validate_python_dependencies()) before touching it. Only a missing or failing environment is (re)provisioned, and it is provisioned into an isolated, never-before-published directory (python3 -m venv + pip install + preflight, all against the isolated path, via subprocess.run inside the function) and published into the per-SHA path with a create-only (no-clobber) renameat2 rename -- the same atomic-publish pattern already used for command/integration runtime materialization in sync-dev-root.sh. The per-SHA path itself is therefore never opened for writing once it is healthy. Both scripts/sync-dev-root.sh and scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh now call this one function through the new `--ensure-python-environment` CLI mode instead of each independently implementing the same reuse/install/preflight/publish decision loop -- closing both the same-SHA re-entry gap (config-drift re-promotion for sync-dev-root.sh, or a plain re-invocation for bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh) and the drift risk of maintaining that mechanism twice.
implementation.fresh_host_provisioning: scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh materializes the immutable command root first, then calls `provision_live_supervisor_config.py --ensure-python-environment --command-root "$COMMAND_ROOT" --python-parent "$SUPERVISOR_PYTHON_PARENT" --requirements "$SUPERVISOR_REQUIREMENTS" --json` to provision $PANTHEON_DEPLOY_ROOT/runtime/supervisor-python/<exact-command-SHA> BEFORE generating the dev-bridge Ed25519 keypair -- which runs under the returned python_executable, never the ambient one, so a fresh host with no ambient cryptography can still bootstrap. scripts/sync-dev-root.sh calls the same CLI mode against the exact candidate being promoted (`--command-root "$candidate_root" --python-parent "$SUPERVISOR_PYTHON_PARENT"`, versioned per exact candidate SHA), parses the JSON python_executable/reused fields, and logs the untouched incumbent root on failure via the wrapping shell `||` handler. Neither script performs venv creation, pip install, dependency preflight, or the atomic publish itself any longer.
implementation.watchdog_restart_preservation: No change was needed in scripts/supervisor_watchdog_install.py or .orchestrator/supervisor_watchdog.py: both already restart the supervisor by re-executing the recorded watchdog.supervisor_command from the live config, so the accepted --python path survives every subsequent restart once promotion renders it correctly.

root_coordination_note: This delivery is source-only, per the SA/SD: exact-version governed promotion after merge, confirming the launched interpreter, automatic pending -> processed admission and canonical readback, a fresh heartbeat, and worker-lease preservation are coordinated by root and are not claimed here.

review_decision.note: Independently verify against this exact head, in particular the structural defect from the second Human/Ops rejection (duplicate policy in bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh:143-239 and sync-dev-root.sh:404-487): (1) the environment provisioning/reuse/publication decision loop now has exactly one implementation -- ensure_supervisor_python_environment() in scripts/provision_live_supervisor_config.py -- and both scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh are thin callers of its new --ensure-python-environment CLI mode; confirm neither script still independently decides reuse, creates a venv, invokes pip, preflights, or performs the renameat2 publish itself (`grep -n 'supervisor_python_verified|candidate_python_dir|python -m venv|pip install' scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh scripts/sync-dev-root.sh` should be empty); (2) no second launcher/dispatcher/cron was added, and bootstrap's keypair sequencing plus sync's candidate/runtime selection remain unchanged at their existing entrypoints; (3) test_ensure_supervisor_python_environment_provisions_and_reuses and test_ensure_supervisor_python_environment_preserves_incumbent_on_failed_preflight in scripts/test_provision_live_supervisor_config.py exercise the shared function directly (fresh provision + publish, same-SHA reuse without touching site-packages, and a failed fresh-candidate preflight leaving an existing per-SHA directory byte-for-byte untouched with no leaked candidate directory); (4) the pre-existing entrypoint tests (test_second_real_run_on_same_sha_reuses_verified_supervisor_python, test_sync_reuses_a_verified_supervisor_python_env_on_same_sha_config_drift) still pass unmodified in behavior against the consolidated wiring, confirming the consolidation is a refactor of the mechanism, not a behavior change; (5) the version-specifier preflight (packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet) and per-SHA read-only-reuse behavior verified in the prior round are unchanged.
